memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "They will be a sign and a wonder to you and your descendants forever. Because you did not serve the Lord your God joyfully and gladly in the time of prosperity, therefore in hunger and thirst, in nakedness and dire poverty, you will serve the enemies the Lord sends against you." — Deut 28:46-48 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Buried in this severe passage is one of the most striking phrases in the whole chapter. The reason given for the coming judgment is not only disobedience, but a particular failure: "because you did not serve the Lord your God joyfully and gladly in the time of prosperity." God noticed not just whether they served Him, but how — with joy, or with grumbling. And He noticed the ingratitude that crept in during good times.

This is deeply searching. It is possible to go through the motions of serving God while our hearts are cold, joyless, and unthankful. God is not merely after outward compliance; He desires glad-hearted worship. And how easily prosperity dulls our gratitude. When life is comfortable, we can quietly forget the Giver and take His gifts for granted.

The warning is clear: joyless, thankless service in the good times is a spiritual danger. When our hearts grow cold toward God amid His blessings, we drift into taking Him for granted.

The gospel calls us to something better. God loves a cheerful heart (2 Cor 9:7), and the more we grasp His grace in Christ, the more joy naturally rises in our service. We serve not a harsh master but a loving Father who gave His Son for us. So cultivate gladness and gratitude, especially in the good times. Serve the Lord with joy, and let thankfulness guard your heart.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I serve God joyfully, or merely out of routine and duty?
2. Has prosperity or comfort dulled my gratitude toward God?
3. What is one thing I can thank God for gladly today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, forgive me for the times my service has been joyless and my heart ungrateful. Fill me with gladness and thankfulness, especially in good seasons, as I serve You. Amen.
